verdict.line: You lose if he lands the Q-stack pull into W stun before level 6; you win any trade you force after his W (Path Maker) is on cooldown.

brief.thesis: K'Sante's whole kit is a forced-engage tool: Q (Ntofo Strikes) builds to a pull, W (Path Maker) charges into a knockback stun, and both feed into R (All Out) resets. He picks the fight, not you. Darius' answer is patience — every stack of Hemorrhage you land for free before he commits is damage he can't take back, and E (Apprehend) lets you yank him into your own combo the instant his engage tools are down.

theirWindow.when: he has 2 Q stacks and W up
theirWindow.what: The 2nd Ntofo Strikes stack fires a shockwave that pulls you in, and Path Maker's charge-up stun follows immediately after. Do not stand in Q range at 2 stacks — back off and let his 14/13/12/11/10s W cooldown run before you re-engage.

yourWindow.when: his W or E just missed or went on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Footwork (E) is only 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s, but Path Maker is his only stun. The moment he whiffs it or dashes away with E, use your own E (Apprehend, 535 range) to pull him back into Q (Decimate) and W (Crippling Strike) before he can reset.

start.why: The highest-performing start into this matchup at 52.7% over 1187 games — the sustain keeps you even through the poke he lands while his Q stacks build.

boots.why: 64.2% pick rate and the higher win rate of the two boot options; his Q (Ntofo Strikes) and autos are his primary poke tool pre-6, and flat physical reduction blunts that chip damage.

core.why: The active dash closes the gap he creates with E (Footwork) and lets you land E (Apprehend) before he resets distance.
Move speed stacking helps you stick through his shield windows instead of losing the chase after a Footwork dash.
Highest win rate of the listed core paths at 67.1% over 70 games — the bleed-out damage reduction lets you survive his All Out burst and still convert with your own stacked Hemorrhage.

situational.when: he is landing his full W stun combo consistently and you need burst survivability
their team stacks magic damage around the K'Sante all-in
you are ahead and want to shred his armor faster than E's passive already does

runes.keystoneWhy: Extended trades are where you win this lane — Conqueror's stacking damage and healing rewards you for staying in range through his Q pokes rather than disengaging, which is exactly the patience this matchup demands. Master-tier data shows a divergence toward Stormraider's Surge (Sorcery) instead — 8,220 games — which suits players who win with the movement speed burst to force the E-pull all-in rather than grinding sustained damage.

summoners.why: The dominant pick at 80.4% and the higher win rate (52.6%) of the three combos. Ghost closes distance to land E (Apprehend) before his W charge-up finishes, and gives you an out if his R (All Out) knockback throws you through a wall into a bad spot.

playing.title: Count his Q stacks constantly
playing.detail: He needs exactly 2 stacks of Ntofo Strikes to fire the pulling shockwave. Track it every time he hits you with Q — at 1 stack you're safe to trade, at 2 stacks you are not.

playing.title: Never stand still for his charge-up
playing.detail: Path Maker's stun only lands if he gets to dash into you after charging. Sidestep the charge window entirely rather than trying to trade through it.

playing.title: Punish his E cooldown windows
playing.detail: Footwork is only 10 to 8 seconds depending on rank. The moment he uses it to reposition or shield, that's your cue to Apprehend and commit.

playing.title: Farm through poke, don't answer it
playing.detail: His early Q trades are meant to bait a response. Take the Doran's Blade sustain and stack Hemorrhage passively with autos instead of matching his aggression stack-for-stack.

playing.title: Hold R for 5 Hemorrhage stacks when possible
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine's true damage scales directly with his bleed stacks, and a kill refreshes its cooldown. Don't burn it early just to start a fight — land Q, W, and autos first.

playing.title: Respect his R from level 6 onward
playing.detail: All Out knocks you through walls and transforms his kit into higher damage with reduced defenses on him. If you're both 6, don't overextend past minions where the knockback can isolate you.

playing.title: Win the side-lane late
playing.detail: Past level 14, your Guillotine refresh and max Hemorrhage stacks out-duel his kit in an isolated 1v1. Look to split rather than group if the game stalls.

brief.patchCaveat: All build paths, runes, boots, summoner spells, and win-rate figures come from measured games on the current patch via OP.GG; the tactical reasoning — when to trade, what each cooldown means for you, and how to sequence the combo — is my own read of the ability interactions.
